title: 10-point 'is your vibe-coded app secure' self-test: HTTPS, hashed passwords, bot protection on forms, expiring sessions, CSRF protection, one-time expiring reset links, limited (not master) DB key, no secrets in logs, billing alerts, automated backups

tools.name: PubNub billing alerts

tools.name: Clever Cloud
tools.detail: Reverse-proxy HTTPS diagram labelled 'Clever Cloud network'

claims: If your app scores under 7 of 10 you 'need to lock in tonight'
A stolen session token should not work forever; sessions must expire
The app's DB key should be a limited key, not the master key
how_to_steps: 2 Store passwords hashed, not plain text
3 Bot protection on signup and public forms
6 Password reset links expire and work once
7 DB key is limited, not master
9 Billing alerts on so you are notified of an attack
on_screen_only: Diagrams: public internet -> reverse proxy -> app VM (HTTPS); scrypt hashing flow; wedding-newsletter signup form with captcha; session/cookie flow; CSRF attack flow (perpetrator -> website visitor -> website); 'Expired reset password link' page; key-types graphic (Super Key, Candidate Key, Primary Key, Unique Key, Alternate Key, Foreign Key, Composite Key, Surrogate Key, Temporal Key); log console; 'Automated backup in action'
cta: Comment how many your app got

relevance.why: Good audit list; billing alerts and backups are operational items vibe coders forget and that cost real money when a bot hammers an endpoint.

implement_score.why: Merge into the same prelaunch security skill; the new work is turning on billing alerts (Supabase/Vercel/Anthropic) and verifying backups/restores for each app.

verify: Supabase anon vs service_role key usage in each app; session expiry defaults in the auth library
Are backups actually restorable (test a restore), not just enabled?

gap.what: Adds operational items missing from liked security videos: billing/usage alerts, automated backups, CSRF, secret-free logs, limited DB key.
